research_questions.md.title: From tissue images to two research questions
research_questions.md.input: Lymphoma tissue images, expert staining grades and supplied subtype labels.

README.md.title: Reproduce a worked example
README.md.input: The published adaptations, their generated inputs and the grading example.

prepare_image_regions.py.title: Mark a core with one click
prepare_image_regions.py.input: A generated tissue-core image and the point you mark.
prepare_image_regions.py.framing: Drawing a rectangle around every core took time and could yield differently sized regions. Could one click mark the centre and let the tool choose a consistent crop?
prepare_image_regions.py.method: Save the crop’s top, bottom, left and right pixel positions. Later steps can use those coordinates to retrieve the same region from the scan.

crop_benchmark.csv.title: Time four ways to collect image regions
crop_benchmark.csv.input: Four extraction methods compared in the submitted thesis.
crop_benchmark.csv.framing: Would one-click marking save time compared with drawing rectangles while still finding the same cores?
crop_benchmark.csv.method: Compare the measured time per sample, precision, recall and manual intervention for four ways of extracting cores.

record_crop_marks.py.title: Save what was marked on a scan
record_crop_marks.py.input: Two named marks on one generated scan, each with a centre and rectangle.
record_crop_marks.py.framing: Could I save the marks separately from the image so they could be reviewed, shared or used again?

extract_labelled_crops.py.title: Turn marked bounds into image files
extract_labelled_crops.py.input: An example image and two labelled sets of pixel bounds.
extract_labelled_crops.py.framing: Once a scan has been marked, can I cut out every region automatically and still know exactly where it came from?

map_crop_to_scan.py.title: Find a smaller crop on the original scan
map_crop_to_scan.py.input: An example box on a reduced image, together with its offset and scale.

filter_tissue_patches.py.title: Keep patches that contain enough tissue
filter_tissue_patches.py.input: Eight squares from a generated mask and a minimum tissue fraction.
filter_tissue_patches.py.framing: A regular grid cuts through empty background as well as tissue. How much tissue should a square contain before I keep it?

summarise_patch_counts.py.title: Spot cores with no usable patches
summarise_patch_counts.py.input: A list of expected cores and the manifest of saved patches.

extract_patch_images.py.title: Save patches with their coordinates
extract_patch_images.py.input: Generated image regions and their measured tissue coverage.

extract_cell_crops.py.title: Cut out separate cell regions
extract_cell_crops.py.input: A generated image and labelled regions, with the allowed size range for retaining a cell.

index_segmented_cells.py.title: Find individual cells on the scan
index_segmented_cells.py.input: Two segmented cells and the coordinates of their containing core.

package_cell_arrays.py.title: Bundle cell records for later analysis
package_cell_arrays.py.input: Two cell IDs, their x/y positions and one feature per cell.

summarise_cells_by_core.py.title: Count cells by their source core
summarise_cells_by_core.py.input: A generated cell index spread across three cores.

compare_image_encodings.py.title: Compare image size and decoded pixels
compare_image_encodings.py.input: The same generated patch saved using PNG and WebP.
compare_image_encodings.py.framing: Can smaller files make it easier to keep the patch collection and still retain the image detail I need?

audit_dataset_structure.py.title: Catch dataset faults before training
audit_dataset_structure.py.input: An expected file inventory and a dataset with deliberate omissions and shape mismatches.

measure_storage_reads.py.title: Time two ways to fetch the same bytes
measure_storage_reads.py.input: Identical generated bytes stored in separate files and in one bundle.

fit_linear_autoencoder.py.title: Learn a shorter description of each patch
fit_linear_autoencoder.py.input: Three generated patches and a two-feature target width.

score_reconstructions.py.title: Find the hardest images to reconstruct
score_reconstructions.py.input: Two pairs of original and reconstructed example arrays.

compare_bottleneck_sizes.py.title: Compare smaller and larger compressed codes
compare_bottleneck_sizes.py.input: The same example input and two candidate widths for its compressed representation.
compare_bottleneck_sizes.py.framing: How much reconstruction quality do I give up when I keep fewer numbers to describe an image?

score_variational_reconstruction.py.title: Separate two parts of reconstruction loss
score_variational_reconstruction.py.input: A generated reconstruction, its target and the statistics of its compressed code.

learn_image_features.py.title: Measure agreement between two image views
learn_image_features.py.input: Paired feature vectors for four generated samples.

prepare_paired_views.py.title: Make two views of the same patch
prepare_paired_views.py.input: One identified patch and two image transformations.

audit_feature_variation.py.title: Find features with little new information
audit_feature_variation.py.input: An example matrix with one column per feature across multiple patches.

fit_shared_view_encoder.py.title: Train one encoder on paired views
fit_shared_view_encoder.py.input: Two generated versions of the same examples and a shared encoder trained for 40 updates.
fit_shared_view_encoder.py.framing: Can one encoder learn to recognise that two altered views came from the same patch?

batch_frozen_features.py.title: Extract features in batches
batch_frozen_features.py.input: Three identified example patches and a fixed feature extractor.

compare_encoder_dimensions.py.title: Estimate how much feature vectors occupy
compare_encoder_dimensions.py.input: Two candidate vector widths and the same set of 30 examples.

standardise_encoder_inputs.py.title: Prepare an image for a fixed encoder
standardise_encoder_inputs.py.input: An RGB image and an encoder’s target dimensions and colour-channel scaling.

benchmark_frozen_features.py.title: Compare features on the same held-out cases
benchmark_frozen_features.py.input: Two generated feature sets, training labels and a shared test split.

measure_feature_separation.py.title: Measure how clearly feature groups separate
measure_feature_separation.py.input: Four example vectors, their group labels and two representations.

project_feature_space.py.title: Plot feature vectors in two dimensions
project_feature_space.py.input: Three labelled example vectors and a fitted two-axis projection.
project_feature_space.py.framing: If I gave each example just two coordinates, would I still be able to see how similar the features are?

check_bag_classifier_on_known_signal.py.title: Check which pooling rule detects a rare signal
check_bag_classifier_on_known_signal.py.input: Sixty-four generated sets of 12 patches with a known planted signal.

export_feature_vectors.py.title: Write a traceable feature table
export_feature_vectors.py.input: Two identified patches, their coordinates and two values per vector.

align_features_to_regions.py.title: Match saved vectors to image regions
align_features_to_regions.py.input: Two sets of records with the same region IDs, in potentially different orders.

check_feature_cache.py.title: Check that saved features still match the job
check_feature_cache.py.input: A cached array, expected encoder name, region order and vector length.

prepare_reference_grades.py.title: Combine the assessors’ grades
prepare_reference_grades.py.input: Three generated assessor ratings for two samples.

assign_validation_folds.py.title: Keep related samples in one validation fold
assign_validation_folds.py.input: Four example samples with known grouping IDs and two destination folds.
assign_validation_folds.py.framing: Can I check the train and test lists in advance so related samples stay together in one fold?

train_scale_graders.py.title: Train a separate grader for each scale
train_scale_graders.py.input: Generated features at two image scales with shared training and test IDs.

save_held_out_grades.py.title: Save predictions on samples left out of training
save_held_out_grades.py.input: Predictions, reference grades and fold assignments for the example cases.

summarise_errors_by_grade.py.title: Find where grades run high or low
summarise_errors_by_grade.py.input: Five example predictions and their reference grades.

compare_experiments.py.title: Compare a change with matched baseline runs
compare_experiments.py.input: Example runs with fold and seed IDs, error, time and memory measurements.

plan_matched_runs.py.title: Plan a fair baseline comparison
plan_matched_runs.py.input: A baseline, two single-change configurations and shared folds and seeds.

verify_run_configuration.py.title: Check that each run used the intended settings
verify_run_configuration.py.input: One planned configuration and the settings that an example run recorded at startup.

summarise_matched_training_traces.py.title: Compare the same training window across runs
summarise_matched_training_traces.py.input: Four matched runs with per-epoch validation scores and elapsed time.

weight_grading_examples.py.title: Adjust which grading examples are sampled
weight_grading_examples.py.input: Four reference grades, their losses and previous weights.

probe_grading_model_with_noise.py.title: Check responses to generated noise
probe_grading_model_with_noise.py.input: Twelve generated signal sets and twelve noise sets for the outside-input class.

compare_assessor_errors.py.title: Put grading error alongside assessor disagreement
compare_assessor_errors.py.input: Two samples with matched assessor grades and model predictions.
compare_assessor_errors.py.framing: How large is model error relative to the differences between two assessors on the same cases?

score_ordinal_agreement.py.title: Account for the size of grading disagreements
score_ordinal_agreement.py.input: Four paired grades where differences of several levels count more than one.

join_subtype_labels.py.title: Match subtype labels to images
join_subtype_labels.py.input: Three example image IDs and a separate list of supplied subtype labels.

audit_cohort_filters.py.title: Record why specimens were kept or excluded
audit_cohort_filters.py.input: Two generated specimens and a set of eligibility rules.

pool_patch_evidence.py.title: Compare ways to combine patch evidence
pool_patch_evidence.py.input: Three generated patch features and three rules for combining them.

batch_variable_patch_sets.py.title: Batch specimens with similar patch counts
batch_variable_patch_sets.py.input: Four specimens that contain different numbers of patches.

predict_subtypes_from_bags.py.title: Train a subtype classifier on sets of patches
predict_subtypes_from_bags.py.input: Two labelled training sets of patches and one generated test set.

compare_spatial_attention.py.title: Test whether patch position changes the score
compare_spatial_attention.py.input: One set of example patch features with two positional arrangements.
compare_spatial_attention.py.framing: Does moving the same patches to different positions change the pooled result?

compare_flat_and_hierarchical_pooling.py.title: Compare pooling cells directly or by patch
compare_flat_and_hierarchical_pooling.py.input: Four generated cell values, their patch memberships and a mask for empty slots.

summarise_validation.py.title: Summarise both tasks by validation fold
summarise_validation.py.input: Example held-out predictions and references for both grading and subtyping.

evaluate_subtype_roc.py.title: See what happens as the subtype threshold moves
evaluate_subtype_roc.py.input: Four example subtype scores and their known binary labels.
evaluate_subtype_roc.py.framing: How does the balance of missed cases and false alarms change as I move the threshold?

compare_fold_class_recall.py.title: Check whether each subtype was recovered in each fold
compare_fold_class_recall.py.input: Two example folds with subtype predictions and reference labels.

estimate_representation_cost.py.title: Estimate the storage saved by keeping features
estimate_representation_cost.py.input: Five hundred example regions, with their raw image dimensions and feature vector size.

rank_accuracy_compute_tradeoffs.py.title: Find the models worth comparing further
rank_accuracy_compute_tradeoffs.py.input: Three candidates described by accuracy, time and memory.

audit_compute_measurements.py.title: Check that timing and memory were recorded
audit_compute_measurements.py.input: Two example runs with their expected time and memory fields.

map_patch_scores.py.title: Place scores back on the image grid
map_patch_scores.py.input: Two example patch scores and their bounds on a four-by-three grid.

render_score_overlay.py.title: Put model scores back on the image
render_score_overlay.py.input: A generated 64 × 48 pixel image with two overlapping scored patches.
render_score_overlay.py.framing: Can a reviewer see where a patch score belongs and tell which image regions were never scored?
render_score_overlay.py.method: Average scores where patch bounds overlap, then render the scores on a shared colour scale. Pixels outside both patches have no score.

summarise_overlay_coverage.py.title: Measure where the overlay has evidence
summarise_overlay_coverage.py.input: Three reference points in a region and their available scores.

explain_prediction.py.title: Inspect which regions the model highlights
explain_prediction.py.input: Four generated image regions and an illustrative two-class model.

model_explanations.md.title: Interpret model highlights cautiously
model_explanations.md.input: Example masks, original scores and scores after dimming selected regions.

test_mask_score_changes.py.title: Compare targeted dimming with a simple control
test_mask_score_changes.py.input: An example explanation mask and an evenly dimmed mask with the same average brightness.
test_mask_score_changes.py.framing: Does dimming selected regions change the score more than dimming the whole input by the same average amount?

compare_patch_perturbations.py.title: Check what changes when one patch is removed
compare_patch_perturbations.py.input: Three generated patches and a fixed rule for scoring the set.

build_cluster_run_manifest.py.title: Give every compute run a stable identity
build_cluster_run_manifest.py.input: Two configurations, two folds and two seeds to expand into a run plan.

resume_chunked_experiment.py.title: Resume work from its last saved chunk
resume_chunked_experiment.py.input: A three-chunk job with an example checkpoint already stored on disk.

collect_fold_results.py.title: Collect results by configuration, fold and seed
collect_fold_results.py.input: Example result files with identifiers and metric records.

find_incomplete_runs.py.title: Find runs that still need attention
find_incomplete_runs.py.input: A planned list of jobs, their start records and any saved final results.

build_grading_table.py.title: Summarise grading errors by image scale
build_grading_table.py.input: A matched example sample with predictions from two image scales.

render_grading_figure.py.title: Turn grading summaries into a reproducible chart
render_grading_figure.py.input: Three image-scale labels with example error estimates and intervals.

run_grading_example.py.title: Follow one grading case into the final figure
run_grading_example.py.input: Two assessor grades for case S02, its fold assignment and feature vectors at three image scales.
run_grading_example.py.framing: Can someone start from one grading error in a chart and trace it back to the original ratings, the held-out case and the prediction?
run_grading_example.py.method: Average the two assessor grades. Fit each scale’s model on other folds, predict S02 in fold 1, then compare that prediction with the reference grade.

bin_patch_distribution.py.title: Show how patches are distributed across cores
bin_patch_distribution.py.input: Saved patch counts for seven example cores.
bin_patch_distribution.py.framing: How many cores yield few patches, and how many yield 200 or more?

grading_figure.svg.title: Compare grading errors across three scales
grading_figure.svg.input: Thirty-six held-out example predictions, twelve for each image scale.

verify_report_assets.py.title: Check which figures and tables made it into the report
verify_report_assets.py.input: Two expected report assets and a generated report directory.

research_limits.md.title: State what the study can establish
research_limits.md.input: The thesis’s internal grading and subtype comparisons and their validation design.

build_benchmark_bags.py.title: Assemble repeatable groups for an external benchmark
build_benchmark_bags.py.input: Example positive and negative patches, split sizes and separate seeds.

compare_benchmark_encoders.py.title: Compare encoders on fixed benchmark splits
compare_benchmark_encoders.py.input: The same labelled training and test sets, with two encoder representations.
